F01.label: Two spaces after sentence-final punctuation (BitcoinTalk; stored by the forum as NBSP+space)

F02.label: Single space after sentence-final punctuation in P2P Foundation posts (platform collapsed whitespace; original form not established)

F03.label: Heavy use of contractions (it's, don't, I'm, you're, it'll, there's)

F04.label: Conditional-politeness frame 'It would be' / 'would be nice'

F09.label: Logical punctuation: period or comma placed outside closing quotation mark

F09b.label: Full-sentence quotation with period inside the closing quotation mark (the exceptions)

F10.label: Numbered lists with '1)' style and bullet lists with '- '

F11.label: Semicolon in prose (very rare: 3 in the whole corpus)

F12.label: Double hyphen used as a dash (no em dash anywhere)

F14.label: Exclamation marks concentrated in release announcements and thanks

F15.label: Non-US spellings (-ise/-isation/-yse, -our, grey, defence, maths, labelled, fulfil)

F16.label: -ize forms (American or Oxford British) and US-only forms (color, gotten)

F19.label: Term formation: 'block chain' as two words, hyphenated 'double-spend' and 'proof-of-work', lower-case 'bitcoin'

F21.label: Upper-case acronyms (TOR, SVN, IRC, CPU, JSON-RPC) and 'SVN rev N' formula

F24.label: Parenthetical asides, often as stand-alone sentences

F26.label: Instructional second person 'you can' / 'you need to'

F27.label: Release-note template: 'Version X is now available', 'Changes:', 'Download:', 'I uploaded ... to SVN'

F29.label: Case-preserving: identifiers keep lower case at sentence start

F30.label: Verdict fragments and very short sentences

F31.label: Numbers: '%' attached without space, 'Nx' multipliers, few thousands separators

F33.label: 'a lot' always two words; 'OK' always upper case
